title: Predecessor credential during a rotation overlap
description: A value that an issuer's rotation procedure has replaced but that the provider documents as still working for a stated overlap or grace period.
semantics: During a documented overlap both the old and the new credential authenticate. Offline text cannot show whether a given occurrence of the old value is inside or past its overlap, so the text alone does not establish that it is dead. What the project should expect of such a value is a policy question, not a provider format fact, and stays unresolved here.

applicability.rationale: Stripe (up to 7 days) and Slack token rotation (grace period on the previous refresh token; existing access token not immediately invalidated) document an overlap. Other providers are not claimed.

evidenceBasis.rationale: The overlap itself is provider-documented (sources). The expectation for a predecessor value is not settled by any provider statement and no maintainer decision with a non-author reviewer is recorded; a recommendation is in the cases. Would settle it: a recorded project-policy decision under docs/governance/evidence-classes.md.

sources.supports: When a key is rotated in the Dashboard both the old and new keys work for up to 7 days.
sources.locator: section 'Rotate safely to avoid downtime', item 'Use the grace period'

sources.supports: Calling oauth.v2.access does not immediately invalidate the existing access token; the used refresh token is revoked after a short grace period.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.
